extracted.intended_audience: researchers in evolutionary biology (authors, reviewers, and recommenders submitting or evaluating preprints)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and platform-level policies for submitting preprints, obtaining public recommendation, and for reviewers/recommenders evaluating preprints in evolutionary biology on the PCI Evolutionary Biology platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive evaluation for public recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints positively evaluated by PCI Evol Biol are publicly recommended and can be published directly in Peer Community Journal, or submitted to PCI-friendly journals or other journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preprint must receive a positive evaluation through the PCI Evol Biol review/recommender process in order to be publicly recommended; recommendation is the platform's endorsement that enables the listed downstream publication options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with guide for authors and editorial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a preprint, authors should carefully read the guide for authors and PCI Evolutionary Biology's community-developed editorial policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow the submission rules, formatting, scope and other requirements set out in the guide for authors and the community editorial policies; failure to comply may affect handling or eligibility for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of acceptable article types
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept most types of articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform is broad in scope, but authors should consult the guide for authors for details on any constrained or excluded article types and for specific submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow guidelines for recommenders and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Evol Biol provides guidelines for recommenders and reviewers that govern how evaluations and recommendations are conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and recommenders should consult and adhere to these guidelines (procedure, confidentiality, ethical expectations, recommended evaluation criteria) when assessing preprints on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome options after recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: A PCI Evol Biol recommendation makes a preprint publicly recommended and eligible for direct publication in the Peer Community Journal or for submission to PCI-friendly journals (or other journals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of the publication pathways enabled by recommendation and consult links describing how to proceed with Peer Community Journal or PCI-friendly journals after receiving a recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and licensing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of comments, reviews and recommendations retain copyright under CC BY for texts published after and including 24/01/2022 and under CC-BY-ND before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should note the license terms that govern reuse and redistribution of text on the platform and ensure any co-authors or contributors understand these terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the work provides innovative models, novel insights, or advances understanding of an important problem in evolutionary biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for clear statements of contribution, novelty relative to existing literature, and whether results materially advance theory, empirical knowledge, or methods; recommendation text on the site frequently highlights 'innovative model', 'new insights', or 'important point'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigor and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods (theoretical models, simulations, experiments, analyses) must be rigorous, appropriate to the question, and correctly applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers check assumptions, modeling choices, statistical analyses, benchmarking, simulation design, and whether methods support the claims; explicit statement of assumptions and justification of approaches is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of presentation and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be clearly written and well-presented so that aims, methods, results and interpretations are understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators note when work is 'clearly presented' or 'methodologically sound'; reviewers expect coherent narrative, transparent reporting of results, and clear linking of evidence to conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of limitations and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should explicitly state limitations, assumptions, and the scope of their conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations commonly highlight appropriate discussion of limitations and suggestions for future work; reviewers expect authors to acknowledge caveats and indicate how results depend on assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness and sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be tested for robustness across parameter choices and model variants (sensitivity analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators favor papers that report sensitivity analyses or show that key findings hold under plausible alternatives; reviewers in examples cite sensitivity analyses as evidence strengthening claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with existing literature and theoretical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies should situate results within the relevant literature and theoretical frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether authors adequately reference prior work, properly frame contributions relative to existing theories, and discuss how findings complement or challenge previous studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality, sampling breadth and empirical support
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical studies should include appropriate sampling, sufficient data, and analyses that justify conclusions (e.g. extensive geographic sampling, adequate genomic coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate dataset size, sampling design, representativeness, and whether data and analyses support the inferences made; limitations of particular markers or sampling schemes should be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate benchmarking and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and correction procedures should be benchmarked and validated under relevant scenarios (e.g. simulation studies, comparison to established methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for carefully designed benchmarks, stated assumptions in simulations, and conservative recommendations where methods show context-dependent performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for the platform and downstream journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should align with the thematic scope and editorial expectations of PCI Evolutionary Biology and potential PCI-friendly journals or the Peer Community Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and recommenders should ensure the manuscript's topic, level, and format fit the platform's scope and consult the list of PCI-friendly journals and editorial policies when considering downstream publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer reviewer engagement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested reviewers should create an account to indicate willingness to review manuscripts for PCI Evol Biol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential reviewers should register on the site (Sign Up) to receive invitations or indicate availability; this is a procedural expectation for community involvement.
